title: Tight line-height (< font content height) places text too high and too tall: negative half-leading is clamped to 0
evidence: text-hero.json: the stat number '12.4k' has lh 44 but the TEXT is y=19 h=56. The real line box is y=24 h=44. As a result the parent's Auto Layout gets pt 19 and spacing 2 instead of 24 and 8, and in the render (and in Figma, where the text height becomes 44) the label moves up about 12px. Same problem for the h1 (lh 79.8, 3 lines = 239px, extracted h=265.6, y off by about 14px), text-inline h1 (y 80 vs about 82.5), text-tw-pricing h1 'Simple pricing' (Tailwind text-6xl with line-height 1: y=90, h=131 instead of 120), '$0'/'$24' (text-5xl), and the '4.9★' tiles in text-mobile-feed. Tailwind's text-5xl…9xl and leading-none/tight are on almost every AI hero.
rootCause: ui.html pageAgent textGeometry(): `hl = Math.max(0, (lh - rects[0].height) / 2)`. When line-height is smaller than the glyph content area, hl should be negative, but it is clamped. The layer then starts at the glyph top instead of the line-box top, and h = glyph extent instead of lines×lh. Also, rects[0] is used as the reference glyph height, so when the first fragment is an inline <code>/<sup>/emoji (different font), hl is wrong as well. One example: the emoji row in text-mobile-feed is at y=17 instead of 13.
verifierNotes:
Confirmed. ui.html pageAgent textGeometry() line 810 has `hl = Math.max(0, (lh - rects[0].height) / 2)`. When line-height is smaller than the font's content area, the half-leading should be negative but is clamped to 0. The layer then starts at the glyph top and is as tall as the glyphs instead of the line box.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs text-hero`. The '.stat .n' text (44px, line-height 1) comes out as TEXT y=19 h=56. The real line box is y=25 h=44, because the stat has 24px padding plus a 1px border. As a result the div.stat Auto Layout gets pt 19 and spacing 2 instead of 25 and 8. In the diff PNG the "TEAMS ONBOARDED" label is visibly doubled, about 12px apart. Real Figma shows the same error: with a 44px lineHeight it makes the text box 44 tall (code.js shapeNode uses textAutoResize, so Figma recomputes the height), places it at the bad y and uses the bad padding and spacing. Figma splits leading evenly above and below the glyphs, like CSS. So the glyphs land about 6px too high and the label about 12px too high. This is a plugin bug, not a renderer artifact. The h1 (3 lines at 79.8px) also comes out as h=265.6 instead of 239.4 and starts about 13px too high.

I tested a corrected fix in a scratch copy of the repo; the real files were not edited. text-hero gives exactly pt 25, spacing 8, text h 44, and the h1 at y=146.1 with h=239.39 (3 × 79.8). diffPct improved on every affected case and nothing got worse:
- text-hero 6.87 → 6.47
- text-docs-mobile 2.04 → 1.71
- text-inline 3.26 → 2.74
- text-mobile-feed 0.97 → 0.82
- text-tw-pricing 1.98 → 1.65 (Auto Layouts detected went from 17 to 19)
- paint-mobile-cards 4.07 → 3.97
- gen-lists, gen-tw-controls, text-overflow and tailwind-snippet did not change
- landing came out at 0.64 with the patch; its unpatched run crashed (missing dev/out/_orig_landing.html temp file), so there is no before value
- no mockErrors in any case

The proposed fix has two problems:
- **Probe inside the target.** It inserts the probe span into the target, or before a text node. That adds an inline 'x' to live content, which can rewrap or shift the line just measured, and forces a layout pass for every text node.
- **Height formula.** It uses lines.length*lh only when line-height is uniform, but never defines that check.

The finding's "simpler alternative" is mostly fine: just drop the Math.max(0, …). But it still uses rects[0] as the reference, so it stays wrong when the first fragment uses a different font (emoji, code, sup).

title: Line-height smaller than the font's content area makes text layers too tall and shifted up, which corrupts gap inference and hug heights
evidence: layout-flex-variants: h1 (52px, line-height 1.1, 2 lines) h=120.19 vs 2×57.2=114.4. layout-grid-stacking: '2.4M' (text-6xl, leading 1 → 60px) h=71. Its hug card (ps=AUTO, gap=3) renders about 11px shorter than the row-span-2 cell in render.png, with a 5px height drift at 390. layout-zorder-transforms: '$0'/'$79' h=43 vs line-height 40, so the column gaps become irregular and the Auto Layout fit fails. In Figma, textAutoResize HEIGHT recomputes the height to lines×lineHeight, so the stored h and y are both wrong.
rootCause: ui.html textGeometry(): `const hl = Math.max(0, (lh - rects[0].height) / 2)` clamps negative half-leading to 0, and h = B - T uses glyph rects instead of the line box.
verifierNotes:
Confirmed, with the code, a harness re-run and a direct Chrome measurement.

**Code.** ui.html textGeometry() (around line 810) does `hl = Number.isFinite(lh) ? Math.max(0, (lh - rects[0].height)/2) : 0; y = T - hl; h = B - T + 2*hl`. Range rects in Chrome always have the font's content-area height (ascent+descent, about 1.17–1.21em for Inter or system fonts), whatever the line-height is. When line-height is smaller than that (Tailwind leading-none/leading-tight, text-5xl..9xl which use line-height:1, h1 {line-height:1.1}), the half-leading is negative. Clamping it to 0 sets y to the glyph top, which sits above the line box, and h to the glyph span, which is taller than lines×lh.

**Chrome probe (scratchpad page).** A 52px Inter h1 with line-height 1.1 and 2 lines: the element box is 0..114.375. The range rects are top -2 / h 61 and top 55.19 / h 61. So the current code gives y=-2 and h=118.19. The unclamped formula gives y≈-0.1 and h≈114.4.

**Harness re-run (layout-flex-variants).** The h1 comes out y=25, h=120.19 against 2×57.2=114.4, so the finding's number reproduces.

**Other cited cases.** The existing JSON agrees:
- layout-grid-stacking: '2.4M' has h=71 against lh 60. Its parent is VERTICAL Auto Layout with primarySizing AUTO, spacing 3 and pt 88. In Figma the text is 60 tall, so the hug card is about 11px shorter than the 218 measured, and the inferred gap of 3 is wrong (the real margin is about 8.5).
- layout-zorder-transforms: '$0', '$24' and '$79' have h=43–45 against lh 40.

**Not a renderer artifact.** dev/render.html lays text out with line-height = lh and auto height, which is the same as Figma's textAutoResize HEIGHT / WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT with PIXELS line height (height = lines×lh, y kept as given). So this is a plugin bug.

**Impact.** Tight headings are on almost every AI-generated landing page, so medium is justified, close to high.

**The proposed fix has a regression.** It takes hl from rects[0] without clamping. Range.getClientRects() on selectNodeContents(el) also returns the border boxes of child inline elements, and isTextBlock() allows painted inline badges or code (boxyInline) in multi-line paragraphs. If the first child is a padded inline span (padding 6px, line-height 20), rects[0] is 30px tall. hl then becomes -5, which pushes y down by 5 and shrinks h. The clamp currently hides this.

**Related bug with the same root cause.** T is a minimum over all rects, including padded inline boxes. My probe paragraph with a padded inline span gives y = 108.38 against a real line top of 114.375, even with normal positive leading.

The corrected fix measures from text-node rects only and allows negative half-leading.

title: text-overflow: ellipsis, overflow:hidden on text elements, and -webkit-line-clamp / Tailwind truncate & line-clamp-N are ignored: the full text overflows over neighbours
evidence: text-overflow.png (inbox): '.from' becomes TEXT WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT 281px wide inside a 219px column and overlaps '9:41'. The subject line is 445–536px wide and covers the main pane. The previews with line-clamp:2 are TEXT h=90 (5 lines) instead of 36, so they overlap the next list item. The clamp3 paragraph is h=144 (6 lines) and runs over the nowrap box. text-tw-pricing: `truncate` loses its '…' and `line-clamp-2` renders 3 lines. text-docs-mobile: `.cmd span{overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap}` becomes a 493px TEXT in a 358px box. Inboxes, tables, cards and sidebars in AI dashboards use these constantly.
rootCause: ui.html walk(): in the isTextBlock branch, when !visual.has the bare TEXT is returned and visual.clip is ignored. textGeometry() measures Range client rects of all content, including the parts hidden by overflow or line clamp. The tree has no truncation fields, and code.js createText/shapeNode never set textTruncation or maxLines.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs text-overflow` (diffPct 1.19, 0 mockErrors) and read the PNGs and the JSON. The bug is real and it is in the plugin.

What the tree shows:
- `.from` "Alexandra Konstantinopolskaya-Whitfield" is TEXT WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT, w=281.05, in a column about 219px wide. It draws over "9:41".
- The two long subject lines are WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT, w=444.97 and w=536, and spill across the main pane.
- The two line-clamp-2 `.preview` texts are HEIGHT h=90 (5 lines) instead of 36. They overlap the next inbox item.
- `.clamp3` is h=144 (6 lines) and runs over `.nowrap-box`.

The original screenshot shows proper ellipses. The render shows all of the overlaps above. The low diffPct only reflects how small the inbox area is compared with the whole page.

Root cause, confirmed in the code:
- ui.html never reads text-overflow or -webkit-line-clamp. A grep finds no truncation, line-clamp or maxLines handling anywhere in the agent.
- `textGeometry()` takes the union of Range client rects. Those rects include content hidden by overflow or by a clamp.
- In `walk()`'s isTextBlock branch, when `!visual.has` the bare TEXT is returned and `visual.clip` is dropped. When the element does paint (like `.nowrap-box`), the clip is kept by the wrapping frame, and the render shows it clipped correctly.
- code.js `shapeNode()` only ever sets textAutoResize to WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT or HEIGHT. It never sets textTruncation or maxLines.

I did not re-run text-tw-pricing or text-docs-mobile. They go through the same code path, so the same result is expected.

The proposed fix has the right idea but is flawed in four ways:
1. `/nowrap|pre/.test(cs.whiteSpace)` also matches `pre-wrap` and `pre-line`, which do wrap.
2. It forces one line height on any clipped `pre`. A `<pre>` with `overflow:auto` (the code block in this very case, and almost every AI-generated page) would collapse to its first line. That is a serious regression.
3. It applies even when nothing overflows. That needlessly changes hugging text to fixed width; the check should use `scrollWidth > clientWidth` and `scrollHeight > clientHeight`.
4. It never handles clip without ellipsis when `!visual.has`. It mentions a frame but does not wire it into `walk()`.

Figma API notes:
- `textTruncation` ('DISABLED' | 'ENDING') and `maxLines` (number >= 1, or null, only used with ENDING) exist on TextNode.
- Truncation has no effect with WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT, so the width must be fixed.
- Figma wraps at word boundaries before it truncates. With maxLines=1, a nowrap line can lose more characters than CSS would. Non-breaking spaces avoid this.

Harness notes:
- The mock's Text class does not validate textTruncation or maxLines. Plain assignment won't throw, but it won't be checked either.
- dev/render.html ignores any truncation field. To confirm the fix with pixels, the harness needs a matching renderer change (that is harness work).

title: Truncated single-line text (text-overflow: ellipsis) overflows its container
evidence: layout-mobile-app: 'Spotify Premium Family subscription renewal' is a WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT TEXT 305px wide inside div.meta 171.7px. render.png shows it running under the amount and chevron, while orig shows 'Spotify Premium Famil…'. This is very common in dashboard tables and list rows.
rootCause: ui.html blockText()/textGeometry() use the full (overflowing) Range width and ignore cs.textOverflow, whiteSpace and overflow. The clipping <b> is lifted, so its overflow:hidden is lost too.
verifierNotes:
I checked this myself and the gap is real. Neither ui.html nor code.js mentions textOverflow, lineClamp, textTruncation or maxLines. The only hit for "ellipsis" is the plugin's own .filename CSS. I re-ran the harness on two cases.

- layout-mobile-app (diff 0.07%): 'Spotify Premium Family subscription renewal' becomes a WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT TEXT 305px wide. Its parent div.meta is 211.7px wide and has clip=false, so the text runs past its box.
- text-overflow (diff 1.19%): the render and orig PNGs show the problem clearly. These items in the 300px sidebar are 281-536px wide and overlap the time labels, the next column and the "Release notes" heading:
  - .from 'Alexandra Konstantinopolskaya-Whitfield'
  - .subject 'Re: Quarterly planning…'
  - '[acme/web] Pull request…'
- -webkit-line-clamp is also ignored. The Range rects include the clamped-away lines, so .clamp3 becomes h=144 (6 lines) instead of 3 lines. .preview (line-clamp 2) becomes h=90 instead of 36. The extra lines spill over the next block ('This line does not wrap' box) and the next list item.

Root cause: textGeometry() takes the union of Range.getClientRects(). For text-overflow and line-clamp this covers the full laid-out text, not what is visible. For a single line it then returns {w: R-L, autoResize: 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT'}. The overflow:hidden on the lifted element is also lost. At ui.html around line 308, a text block with !visual.has is returned as a bare TEXT and visual.clip is ignored. code.js shapeNode()/createText() have no truncation support.

This is common in AI-generated dashboards, inboxes, tables and cards (Tailwind `truncate` and `line-clamp-N`). The result is overlapping text, but only when the content is actually long, so I rate it medium.

The proposed fix is mostly right but has four flaws:
1. It would force every ellipsis element to the content-box width even when the text fits. That breaks the auto-width hug for short labels like 'Jordan Miles'. It should apply only when the text actually overflows.
2. Requiring whiteSpace === 'nowrap' is too narrow. 'pre' and text-wrap-mode nowrap also produce single-line truncation; checking for a single measured line is more robust.
3. For line-clamp it must also fix g.h, which is wrong (it includes the hidden lines), not only set maxLines.
4. It misses the looseText path, where the ellipsis is on a parent with mixed children.

Two harness notes:
- The fix can't be checked visually until dev/render.html honors truncate/maxLines. Today it only uses white-space pre or pre-wrap.
- mock-figma.js does not validate textTruncation/maxLines. Setting them on its class instance just adds the properties, so no mock errors appear.

On Figma's text handling: Figma has no nowrap, so with maxLines=1 it breaks at a word and shows 'Spotify Premium…' instead of the browser's 'Spotify Premium Famil…'. This is a small, acceptable difference.

title: An inline-block/inline-flex child inside a paragraph splits it into loose TEXT layers that ignore the first-line offset, so text overlaps
evidence: text-mobile-feed@390.render.png: in the post body ('Conversion is up +18% week over week… '), the text after the badge is TEXT x=0 w=334 although it starts mid-line at about x=167. It overlaps the 'Conversion is up' line and the badge, rewraps, and '#buildinpublic' lands on its own line. Tailwind `inline-flex items-center gap-1` links with an arrow icon, inline badges and inline-block avatars inside sentences are very common in v0/Claude output.
rootCause: ui.html isTextBlock(): it returns false as soon as any child has display other than inline/contents. walk() then goes to childrenOf() → looseText() for each text node. textGeometry() with lines.length>1 returns `x: box.x, w: box.w` (the parent content box), which assumes the text starts at the left edge on its first line. The first-line indent caused by the preceding inline-block is lost.
fix:
Main fix, in ui.html: split multi-line text whose first line starts after the line's left edge.

1. **New helper `splitFirstLine(tn, start, end, wrapBox, cs)`.** Use it from `looseText()`, and from a range-based variant of `textGeometry()`.
   - Build a range over the trimmed text (as `textGeometry` already does). Get its line boxes (rects with width > 0.5, grouped by line midpoint).
   - Only split when ALL of these hold:
     - lines > 1
     - `cs.textAlign` is start/left/justify (for center/right, keep the current behaviour)
     - `firstLineLeft > wrapBox.x + 1`
2. **Find the first character on line 2 with a binary search over offsets k in (start, end]:**
   - `P(k)` = `range(tn, start, k)` covers more than one distinct line (rects width > 0.5). `P` is monotone, so binary search works.
   - The smallest k with `P(k)` true gives `cut = k - 1`.
   - If `tn.data.charCodeAt(cut)` is a low surrogate (0xDC00–0xDFFF), use `cut - 1`.
3. **Build two layers:**
   - `segsA = toSegments([{raw: tn.data.slice(0, cut), el: parent}])`, placed by `range(start, cut)` with `autoResize 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT'`. Trailing spaces are already stripped by `toSegments`.
   - `segsB = toSegments([{raw: tn.data.slice(cut), el: parent}])`, placed with `x = wrapBox.x`, `w = wrapBox.w`, `y` from `range(cut, end)` plus the half-leading, `autoResize 'HEIGHT'`.
   - `looseText` returns both layers. `childrenOf` must push an array, e.g. `for (const t of [].concat(looseText(...) || [])) out.push(t)`.
   - The last line needs no special case, because Figma lays text out from the left.
4. **Inline elements handled by `blockText`.** When `el` is `display:inline` (or `inline` wrapped by `walk`) and its text wraps:
   - Use the content box of the nearest block-level ancestor as `wrapBox`, not `contentBox(el)`. `contentBox(el)` is the bounding box of the line fragments.
   - Apply the same first-line split over the element's range. This works across child nodes: do the binary search over a flattened list of (textNode, offset) positions from `gatherRuns`, cut the runs at that point, and call `toSegments` on each half.
   - Skip this when the element paints a box (`visual.has`). Those stay framed as today.

Optional, safe subset of part (1): treat an inline-block or inline-flex child as inline in `isTextBlock` only when ALL of these hold:
- it contains only text/inline markup (recursive scan, no ATOMIC tags)
- `lineCount(c) === 1`
- it has no background, border or shadow (`!hasPaint`)
- horizontal padding + border + margin is under 1px

Typical examples are `<span class="inline-block">`, and gradient-clip words in hero headings (bg-clip-text; the gradient is still picked up by `clipGradient`). Merging those is exact.

Keep painted badges (padding > 0 or a background) as separate frames, and rely on the split above. Do NOT merge them into the text with a background rect until there is a way to reserve the padding width.

Regression check: text that starts at the line's left edge does not meet the gating conditions, so it is never split. Single-line text keeps the existing `alignBox` and WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT path. The only change for wrapped text after an inline-block, icon or `text-indent` is the extra first-line layer.

This one is fine because it ends mid-line. - FRAME `span.badge-inline` at x=122.8, y=24.5. - TEXT "week over week. Huge thanks … copy." at x=0, y=21.75, w=334, h=67.5, HEIGHT. In the browser it starts at about x=172 on line 2. - WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT TEXTs for #buildinpublic and "Read the write-up". **What the render shows:** "week over week. Huge" is drawn on top of "Conversion is up" and the badge. The rest wraps one line earlier, so "#buildinpublic Read the write-up" sits by itself on a line with empty space to the left. The text is visibly broken. **Root cause (confirmed in the code):** 1. `isTextBlock()` returns false when any child is not inline/contents, or is an ATOMIC tag. That includes inline-block badges, inline-flex links, and inline `` icons. 2. `walk()` then calls `childrenOf()`, which calls `looseText()` for each text node. 3. `textGeometry()` with `lines.length > 1` returns `x: wrapBox.x, w: wrapBox.w` and drops the first line's starting x. **Wider trigger than reported:** the same thing happens with: - an inline svg/img icon before wrapping text - `text-indent` on the first loose text - a `display:inline` element that starts mid-line and wraps. But it is not gated: it would also split ordinary text that starts at the line start. It ignores surrogate pairs (emoji such as 🎉 sit right in this text). And it does not cover inline elements handled by `blockText`. - **Part (1)**, merging painted inline-block badges into the paragraph's segments plus a background rect, is risky. Figma text has no inline padding, so each badge's horizontal padding (16px here) disappears. Following text shifts left, wrap points can change, and the DOM-measured background rect no longer sits under its text. The rect also relies on a mechanism ("the inline-background finding") that does not exist in ui.html today. Merging is only exact when the inline-block adds no horizontal space and draws no box.

title: Backgrounds, borders and padding of inline <code>/<mark>/<kbd>/badge spans are dropped inside wrapping paragraphs, and the missing padding changes line breaks
evidence: text-inline.render.png: in the paragraph with `npm i -g @acme/cli`, `acme login` and `~/.acme/config.json`, the grey code pills and the yellow <mark> are gone, and 'the' jumps up to line 1 because 4×12px of inline padding disappeared. The kbd keys lost their borders. In the .note box, the ACME_ENV code pill is gone. Inline code is in virtually every docs/README-style AI page.
rootCause: ui.html isTextBlock(): when `boxyInline && lineCount(el) > 1`, everything is merged into one TEXT. toSegments()/segStyle() carry only font, fill and decoration, so the inline box (background, border, radius, padding, margin) is discarded, and the inline padding no longer contributes to the horizontal advance.
fix:
Corrected fix. All changes are in ui.html; code.js needs no change, because createText() already applies each segment's letterSpacing with setRangeLetterSpacing.

1) **Collect painted inline elements.** In isTextBlock()'s scan, when hasPaint(ccs) is true, push c into a list such as `S.inlineBoxes.set(el, [...])`. Do this only on the `lineCount(el) > 1` path, since that is the only one that merges the paragraph.

2) **Map elements to character ranges.** In toSegments(), keep a running output offset. For each run, after collapsing whitespace and stripping the leading space, record `run.start` and `run.end`. For each painted element E, its range is `start = min(run.start)` and `end = max(run.end)` over runs where `E.contains(run.el)`. Clamp `end` to the final string length after the trailing trim.

3) **Keep the line breaks.** For each E, read its computed style `cs`. Let `L = marginLeft + borderLeftWidth + paddingLeft` and `R = paddingRight + borderRightWidth + marginRight`.
   - Add R to the letter spacing of character `end - 1`.
   - If `start > 0`, add L to the letter spacing of character `start - 1`. If `start == 0`, shift the TEXT node's x by L and shrink its width by L.
   - To do this, split the containing segment so the character becomes a one-character segment with `letterSpacing = base + extra`. Figma adds letter spacing after each glyph, which matches where the padding sits in CSS.
   - Only the first and last characters of E get extra spacing, which matches box-decoration-break: slice. If E uses `box-decoration-break: clone`, skip this compensation, or split per fragment.

4) **Emit the boxes.** For each E, call `E.getClientRects()`, not a Range's rects. These are border-boxes per line fragment, including padding and border, and already sliced. For each fragment, emit a node:
   - `{type:'RECT', x: r.left - ox, y: r.top - oy, w: r.width, h: r.height}`
   - `fills: backgroundFills(cs, fragBox)`
   - `effects: parseShadows(cs.boxShadow)`
   - `stroke: borders(cs)`. On the first fragment, set the right side's weight to 0; on the last fragment, set the left side's weight to 0; on middle fragments, set both to 0. Figma supports per-side stroke weights via strokeLeftWeight/strokeRightWeight; check that code.js passes the per-side weights through.
   - `radii`: the first fragment gets only topLeft and bottomLeft, the last gets only topRight and bottomRight, and a single fragment gets all four.
   Skip fragments narrower than 0.5px. If the cumulative content offset at the start of E's line isn't known, skip the per-fragment width adjustment.

5) **Placement and z-order.**
   - Paragraph without its own visual (the `!visual.has` branch in the element-to-node function): return a wrapper FRAME `{name: nameFor(el), ...box, fills: [], children: [...rects, text]}`. Use parent-relative coordinates for the frame and frame-relative coordinates for the children. Make it vertical Auto Layout with zero padding, the TEXT as the only in-flow child set to stretch, and the rects marked `absolute: true`. place() already sets layoutPositioning = 'ABSOLUTE', so the text keeps resizing with the layout.
   - Paragraph with a visual (the .note case): push the rects into the existing frameNode children before t, marked `absolute: true`. tryAutoLayout() already ignores absolute kids.
   - In both cases the rects come before the TEXT in the children list, so they paint underneath it.

6) **Regression guard.** Only take this path when lineCount > 1, as today. Leave single-line paragraphs on the existing separate-box path. Name each rect after its tag (e.g. "code bg" or "mark bg") so users can find and delete them.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs text-inline` (diff 3.24%, 0 mock errors) and compared text-inline.orig.png with text-inline.render.png. The finding holds.
- **First paragraph:** the grey pills behind `npm i -g @acme/cli`, `acme login` and `~/.acme/config.json` are gone, and so is the yellow <mark> background. Line 1 now ends with "...redirected to the" where the original ends with "to", so the line breaks have moved. The pink monospace text colour is kept.
- **kbd keys:** in the second paragraph the ⌘ and K keys lost their border, background and radius, and the line wraps differently ("palette" moves up).
- **.note box:** the `ACME_ENV=preview` pill is gone and the text after it moves left.

Root cause, confirmed in ui.html:
- isTextBlock() sets boxyInline when hasPaint(ccs) is true and then returns `lineCount(el) > 1`. So any paragraph of two or more lines is merged into one TEXT node built by gatherRuns() and toSegments().
- segStyle() records only font, size, fill, decoration, letterSpacing, lineHeight and textCase. The inline element's background, border, radius and shadow are never emitted, and nothing makes up for its horizontal padding, border and margin.
- Single-line paragraphs are not affected: lineCount 1 makes isTextBlock return false, and each inline box becomes its own layer.

Severity is medium, not high. Text and colours stay correct, so the page is not broken, but the pills are clearly missing and the line breaks and paragraph heights shift. This happens on docs, README and changelog pages, which AI tools generate a lot; it is less common on marketing landing pages.

The proposed fix has a real bug. It measures fragments with `range.selectNodeContents(c); range.getClientRects()`. In ui.html textGeometry(), multi-line branch: run this only when `/balance|pretty/.test((cs.textWrapStyle||'') + ' ' + (cs.textWrap||''))`. Do not apply it to plain CENTER text.

Compute a safe greedy width W with a new helper, balancedWidth(target, box):
1. Walk the text nodes of target (or use target itself if it is a text node). For each /\S+/ word, make a Range and get its single client rect. If any word yields 0 or 2+ rects (hyphenated or split word), return 0.
2. Group the words into lines by vertical midpoint. Keep left, right and the word list for each line.
3. maxLine = max over lines of (right - left).
4. join = min over i < last of (width of line i + inter-word gap + width of the first word of line i+1). Take the gap from the distance between two words on line i, or 0 if the line has one word.
5. If join - maxLine < 2, no single width reproduces the breaks (typical for `pretty`). Return 0, which keeps the current behavior.
6. Otherwise return ceil(min(box.w, maxLine + (join - maxLine)/2)). This is the midpoint of the safe interval, which leaves room for small metric differences between Chrome and Figma on both sides.

In textGeometry, if W is non-zero and W < box.w - 1:
- set x = CENTER ? box.x + (box.w - W)/2 : RIGHT ? box.x + box.w - W : box.x
- return {x, y, w: W, h, align, autoResize: 'HEIGHT', wrapX: box.x, wrapW: box.w}
Otherwise return the current full-box geometry.

Regression guard in fitLayout(frame, kids, dir, ...): if it returns null and some kid has wrapW, reset each such kid to x = wrapX, w = wrapW (convert to the frame's local coordinates the same way the kid's x was converted) and call fitLayout again. This keeps Auto Layout and gives up the balanced breaks only in that rare case. markStretch needs no change: a narrowed text has w != inner, so it is not stretched, and the fallback restores stretch eligibility. code.js needs no change; wrapX and wrapW are extra properties that only ui.html uses and can be deleted before posting.

Optional exact alternative for `pretty`, or when W is 0: insert U+2028 (Figma's soft line break) at the measured break offsets and keep w = box.w. This reproduces any breaks exactly, at the cost of fixed breaks when the text is edited later. Offer it only as a separate option.

title: Gradient text on an inline span: gradient transform is computed in the span's box but Figma applies it relative to the whole TEXT node

The TEXT node is 358×78, so in Figma the blue→pink ramp is spread over the full node box instead of the span's glyphs. rootCause: ui.html clipGradient(): `gradientPaint(..., r.width, r.height)` uses the clipping element's rect. code.js setRangeFills applies paint transforms in the TEXT node's unit space.
fix:
All changes are in `ui.html`. `code.js` needs none.

**1. Return the box with the paint, in page coordinates.**

In `clipGradient(el)`, return the paint together with its box: `{ paint, box }`.
- For a non-inline clip element, `box` is its padding box: the border box minus the border widths.
- For an inline clip element, measure its line fragments: create a range on the element, take `range.getClientRects()`, keep rects with width and height above 0.5, and group them by line midpoint (as `lineCount` does). Each fragment k gets `{x_k, y_k, w_k, h_k}` and an offset `o_k`, the sum of the widths of the earlier fragments. The virtual box is `W = Σ w_k`, `H = max h_k`.
- Build the base paint as `gradientPaint(img, W, H)` for an inline element, or `gradientPaint(img, box.w, box.h)` for a block one.

In `segStyle`, store the result as `fill = Object.assign({}, paint, { _clip: { el: e, frags } })`.
- For a block element, `frags` holds one fragment: `{x: box.x, y: box.y, w: box.w, h: box.h, o: 0}`.
- `_clip` must not be included in `style.key`. Build the key from a copy of the style without `_clip`, and add the clip element identity to the key so segments from the same element still merge.

**2. Post-pass after geometry: `localizeGradients(segs, g)`.**

Call it in `blockText` and `looseText` after `textGeometry` and before `textNode`/`shift`. There `g` is in page coordinates.

For each segment with `fill._clip`:
- Split the segment's text into one piece per line fragment. To find the boundaries, walk the clip element's text nodes with a one-character Range, get each character's line from its rect midpoint, and map back by counting characters as `toSegments` collapses whitespace. If the mapping is ambiguous, skip the split and use only fragment 0's mapping for the whole segment.
- For each piece on fragment k, re-express the transform in the TEXT node's unit space. Use `T0` (the base `gradientTransform`, 2x3 for a virtual box of size `W×H`) and `Xn, Yn, Wn, Hn = g.x, g.y, g.w, g.h`.
  - A node-unit point `(u, v)` is at page position `(Xn + u·Wn, Yn + v·Hn)`.
  - Its virtual-box unit coordinates are:
    - `s = (Xn + u·Wn − x_k + o_k) / W`
    - `t = (Yn + v·Hn − y_k) / H`
  - So `M = [[Wn/W, 0, (Xn − x_k + o_k)/W], [0, Hn/H, (Yn − y_k)/H], [0, 0, 1]]`.
  - The new transform is `T0 · M` (3x3 product, drop the last row).
  - Code sketch: `const mul = (A, M) => [0, 1].map((i) => [A[i][0]*M[0][0], A[i][1]*M[1][1], A[i][0]*M[0][2] + A[i][1]*M[1][2] + A[i][2]]);`
- Delete `_clip` from the fill.
- Merge adjacent segments only if their style keys and transforms are equal.
- Apply this to `GRADIENT_RADIAL` and `GRADIENT_ANGULAR` paints too. They use the same unit-space convention, so the same `M` is correct.

**3. Strip in `textNode`.**

In `textNode(segs, g)`, as a safety net, delete any remaining `fill._clip`. This covers the form-control path (`textNode` calls around lines 924–932), whose `g` is not in page coordinates; those segments keep the element-relative transform as before. No unknown property must ever reach `setRangeFills`.

**Notes**
- Figma's text box can differ slightly from the measured `g` after a WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT resize, because the font metrics differ. The resulting error is small, compared with the current reversed or near-solid ramps.
- No regression for whole-element gradient text such as the `text-hero` h1. There `M` becomes almost identity, plus a small padding/glyph-box correction.
- Verification: `render.html` draws gradient text per span, so the harness cannot check this. Check in real Figma or by computing colour samples from the node-space transform.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs text-docs-mobile -w 390` (diffPct 11.01). The Hebrew paragraph comes out as align=LEFT, autoResize=HEIGHT, x=16, w=358, h=81.58. In orig.png the paragraph is right-aligned; in render.png all three lines are left-aligned. So the alignment bug is real and comes from the plugin.

It uses no new Figma API: only textAlignHorizontal LEFT/RIGHT/CENTER/JUSTIFIED. title: Font substitution is not reflected in layout: the page is measured with SF Pro/Helvetica (system-ui, -apple-system, ui-sans-serif) but Figma gets Inter, so lines re-wrap
evidence: Code reasoning plus text-tw-pricing.json: Tailwind's default stack gives segments family '-apple-system'. code.js resolveFont maps it to Inter, while the browser measured line breaks and the WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT widths with SF Pro. Text that fills its width (headings, nav, buttons) then wraps differently or overflows in Figma. The same applies to missing families ('Totally Missing Font', … Georgia in text-hero): the browser falls back to Georgia but Figma picks the first available family of the GENERIC_FAMILIES.serif list. The harness cannot show this (see the harness finding about fonts).
rootCause: The ui.html agent measures the DOM with whatever font the OS/browser picked. code.js resolveFont picks a different font, and nothing reconciles them.
fix:
Make the browser lay text out with the font Figma will actually pick, using one shared resolution step.

1) Send Figma's font list to the UI (code.js, ES2017). On startup or on 'import-start', call `buildFontIndex()` and post `{type:'fonts', families: Array.from(idx.values()).map(function(e){return e.family;})}`. Also send the resolved generics: `generic = {sans: first of GENERIC_FAMILIES.sans that idx has, serif: ..., mono: ...}`. The UI passes `opts.figmaFonts = {families, generic}` in the 'extract' message. If the list hasn't arrived, use `{sans:'Inter', serif:'Noto Serif', mono:'JetBrains Mono'}`.

2) Mirror resolveFont in pageAgent as `figmaFamilyFor(families)`. Use the same alias table: copy GENERIC_ALIASES/GENERIC_FAMILIES into the agent, or keep one source and serialise it into opts. Walk the stack: the first entry Figma has wins; a generic alias maps to `opts.figmaFonts.generic[alias]`; 'skip' entries are skipped; anything else falls back to generic.sans.

3) In the extract handler, after `settle()` and before `extract()`, when `opts.matchFigmaFonts !== false` (default on, exposed as an option):
- Skip whole subtrees of svg/math/script/style elements.
- For each element with a direct non-empty text node child, or a form control, read `cs = getComputedStyle(el)` and `fams = parseFamilies(cs.fontFamily)`.
- If `fams[0]` is a family the page loaded itself (`[...document.fonts].some(f => f.status === 'loaded' && unquote(f.family).toLowerCase() === fams[0].toLowerCase())`), leave the element alone. This protects icon fonts and real webfonts.
- Otherwise set `target = figmaFamilyFor(fams)`. If `target.toLowerCase() !== fams[0].toLowerCase()`, call `el.style.setProperty('font-family', '"' + target + '", ' + cs.fontFamily, 'important')` and add target to the set `needed`.
- Pseudo-elements inherit the inline value unless they declare their own font-family, which is the case for icon pseudos, so leave those as they are.

4) Load the needed families so the browser lays out with real metrics:
- For each target in `needed` that Figma has but `document.fonts.check('16px "' + target + '"')` reports missing, inject `<link rel=stylesheet href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=' + encodeURIComponent(target) + ':ital,wght@0,100..900;1,100..900&display=block">`.
- Wait for each link's load/error event, then run `Promise.all` of `document.fonts.load(weight + ' ' + (italic ? 'italic ' : '') + '16px "' + target + '"')` for each (weight, italic) pair collected in the walk.
- Wrap all of this in `Promise.race` with a 4 s timeout, then `await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame)` twice so layout reflows. Only then call `extract()`.
- If loading fails (CSP font-src, offline), the original stack is still listed after the target, so layout falls back to what it was. That is no worse than today.
- networkAccess is already '*' in manifest.json.

5) The recorded segments will then read families `[target, ...original]`. resolveFont hits target first, so Figma and the measurement agree.

Notes:
- Fixed-size frames are measured after the reflow too, so containers widen along with their text. That is the intended Figma result.
- In the harness, the original screenshot is taken without this step, so case diffs will grow wherever fonts were swapped. Run the comparison against a reference with the same swap applied, or accept a visible font change as expected.
verifierNotes:
The gap is real. I checked it against the code and measured it in Chrome; the harness can't show it.

Code:
- ui.html segStyle records `parseFamilies(cs.fontFamily)`, which is the declared stack, not the font the browser actually used. Text geometry (x/y/w/h, and the line breaks behind it) comes from Range rects laid out in the browser's font.
- In code.js, resolveFont maps the first alias in the stack ('-apple-system', 'system-ui', 'ui-sans-serif', 'segoe ui', ...) to GENERIC_FAMILIES.sans[0], which is Inter. Nothing makes the two sides agree.
- shapeNode then sets `textAutoResize = 'HEIGHT'` with the measured width for multi-line or aligned text, so Figma re-wraps in Inter. Single-line 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT' text grows wider instead.
- dev/out/text-tw-pricing.json confirms segments carry ['-apple-system', 'system-ui', 'Segoe UI', ...] and ['ui-monospace', 'SFMono-Regular', 'Menlo'].

Measurement: I compared DOM span widths in headless Chrome on macOS, which is the same engine as Figma's plugin iframe.
- Inter is 4.1-4.6% wider than system-ui (SF Pro) at weight 400 and 0.1-0.8% wider at 700.
- It is 6-8% wider than Helvetica/Arial at 400.
- Against Georgia it is +6-8% at 400 and -4 to -6% at 700.

So body text, buttons and nav measured in SF Pro come out about 4% wider in Figma. That gives extra wrapped lines in HEIGHT texts, which collide in absolutely placed parents or make auto-layout frames taller. Shrink-to-fit containers (buttons, badges) end up too tight or off-center. Bold headings are barely affected. That fits "medium": noticeable and common, not catastrophic.

Harness: render.html (line 117) re-renders with the same family list as the original, so orig and render use the same font and the diff stays clean. The mock font list also has no SF Pro. Evidence is code plus measurement, not a harness diff.

Corrections to the evidence:
- Chrome does not recognise `-apple-system` (it measured the same as the default serif). In real stacks the browser actually lands on BlinkMacSystemFont or system-ui (SF Pro). The mismatch stands.
- The serif claim only holds when Figma lacks Georgia. In the browser build Georgia is usually missing (not a Google Font), so Figma picks Noto Serif while the browser shows local Georgia.

Problems with the proposed fix:
1. It hardcodes 'Inter', 'JetBrains Mono' and "first entry of the serif list" in the agent. GENERIC_FAMILIES.serif[0] is Georgia, which is local in the browser but often missing in Figma, so the fix would do nothing for serif. The target must come from Figma's real font list via the same resolution code.js uses.
2. It only checks whether the first entry is a generic name. It misses named fonts the browser has locally but Figma lacks, and the reverse.
3. It must not touch icon fonts or other page-loaded webfonts. Overriding those would break glyph measurement.
4. `document.fonts.ready` can resolve before an injected `<link>` has even loaded its CSS, so waiting on it is not enough.

title: text-indent and font-variant: small-caps are not mapped
evidence: text-hero: the `.quote p { text-indent: 2em }` paragraphs lose their first-line indent (render.png), and `.caps { font-variant: small-caps }` renders as normal mixed case.
rootCause: ui.html segStyle()/textNode() never read cs.textIndent or cs.fontVariantCaps. code.js has no paragraphIndent or SMALL_CAPS handling.
verifierNotes:
I checked this myself. A grep of ui.html and code.js finds no reference to textIndent, fontVariantCaps, paragraphIndent or SMALL_CAPS. segStyle() (ui.html ~l.725) sets textCase only from TEXT_CASE[cs.textTransform]. textNode()/blockText() never read text-indent, and createText() in code.js never sets paragraphIndent. I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs text-hero`: diffPct 6.87, 0 mock errors. In dev/out/text-hero.json the ".caps" TEXT has textCase:null, and neither ".quote p" TEXT carries any indent. Cropped PNGs back this up. In orig.png both quote paragraphs start with a 2em first-line indent and ".caps" is drawn as small caps. In render.png both paragraphs start flush left, so line breaks shift ("was / not" becomes "the / tooling"), and the caps line is ordinary mixed case. Font fallback adds some noise, but the missing indent and caps are real plugin gaps. The renderer is not the cause. The idea behind the fix is right, but it has five problems: 1. textNode() has no `cs`, and the indent must not go there. looseText() also uses textNode() for text runs that can start mid-block, where an indent would be wrong. 2. getComputedStyle keeps text-indent percentages as "10%", so parseFloat gives the wrong value. 3. Negative values (the old `text-indent:-9999px` hiding trick, hanging indents) must not be passed through. Figma's paragraphIndent is not meant to be negative. 4. Figma indents every paragraph, i.e. after every '\n'. CSS indents only the first line of the block, not lines after a
. 5. The proposed ordering lets small-caps override text-transform:uppercase. In CSS, uppercase + small-caps shows full-size capitals, so UPPER must win. Two smaller points. Fonts without an smcp feature may not support SMALL_CAPS in Figma, so the call should be guarded. The harness also needs changes before this can be verified: dev/mock-figma.js setRangeTextCase only accepts ORIGINAL/UPPER/LOWER/TITLE, so it would report SMALL_CAPS as a mockError. dev/render.html ignores paragraphIndent and would need to map SMALL_CAPS to font-variant-caps. That is harness work and does not argue against the fix. Low severity is correct: AI-generated landing pages and dashboards rarely use text-indent or small-caps.

title: sup/sub (vertical-align) lose their baseline shift and render as small text on the baseline
evidence: text-inline: 'H₂O' and 'πr²' render as 'H2O'/'πr2' with the small digit sitting on the baseline. text-docs-mobile: footnote markers '1' and '[2]' are on the baseline (render.png).
rootCause: ui.html segStyle() ignores cs.verticalAlign. The Figma plugin API has no settable baseline shift (TextNode.openTypeFeatures, which reports SUPS/SUBS, is read-only).
verifierNotes:
I confirmed this independently. ui.html segStyle(el, cs, colorOverride) builds font, size, fill, decoration, letterSpacing, lineHeight and textCase. It never reads cs.verticalAlign, never checks the element tag, and never looks at a relative top offset. There is no other "baseline", "verticalAlign", "SUPS" or "SUBS" handling anywhere in ui.html or code.js.

I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs text-inline` (diffPct 3.24, 0 mockErrors). In the tree JSON the paragraph segments are 'Water is H' (16/28), '2' (11.2/19.6), 'O and the area…' (16/28), '2' (11.2/19.6). The render.png shows "H2O" and "πr2" with the small digit sitting on the baseline, which matches the evidence. This is not a renderer artifact: Figma would draw the same thing, because the run carries no baseline shift.

The Figma plugin API has no settable baseline shift. TextNode.openTypeFeatures (SUPS/SUBS) can only be read; I am not confident a range setter exists, so the fix must not rely on one.

Problems with the proposed fix:
(a) A separate absolutely positioned TEXT plus letterSpacing compensation is fragile. It breaks editing and reflow, needs layoutPositioning ABSOLUTE inside auto-layout parents, drifts as soon as the text is edited or the font metrics differ, and makes simple footnotes noticeably more complex. I advise against it.
The "keep the parent lineHeight" part is mostly a no-op. A smaller per-range lineHeight does not enlarge the Figma line, so it only helps keep things consistent.
It also misses that Tailwind's preflight styles sup/sub with vertical-align: baseline; position: relative; top: -0.5em / bottom: -0.25em, and with line-height: 0. A check on cs.verticalAlign alone would therefore miss every Tailwind page. Detection must look at the tag or at relative offsets.

Impact is cosmetic and rare (chemical formulas, exponents, footnote markers, ™/® marks), so severity low is right.

title: Text-only elements with padding are lifted to bare TEXT, dropping their box; siblings that kept a frame no longer align, so the list loses Auto Layout
evidence: layout-legacy-structures: aside ul has no layout. The active item is FRAME a.active at x=0 (it has a background), while 'Orders', 'Customers' and 'Reports' are TEXT at x=12 because their padded <a> boxes were discarded. The same happens with layout-zorder-transforms' 'Settings' row (the last row has no border). This pattern is common in sidebars, tabs and menus with one highlighted item.
rootCause: ui.html walk(): in the isTextBlock branch, `if (!visual.has) return [Object.assign(t, common)]` positions the text at its glyph box and forgets the element's border box and padding.
verifierNotes:
I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs layout-legacy-structures`: diffPct 1.25, 0 mock errors, 47 auto layouts. In dev/out/layout-legacy-structures.json, `FRAME ul` (16,69 208x132) has no `layout`. Its children are `FRAME a.active` at (0,0,208,33) with VERTICAL padding 8/12, followed by three TEXT nodes at x=12, y=41/74/107, w=184, h=17. That is exactly the reported situation.

Root cause is in ui.html walk(). In the isTextBlock branch, `if (!visual.has) { shift(t, ox, oy); return [Object.assign(t, common)]; }` returns only the glyph box, so the `<a>` border box and its padding (8px 12px) are lost. The `<li>` wrapper is then removed by the "plain && kids.length === 1" path. fitLayout() then checks the cross axis. `before` is [0,12,12,12] and `after` is [0,12,12,12], so the start and end alignments both fail. In the CENTER branch, diff is [0,0,0,0], which passes. The main axis fails, though. The gaps are 41-33=8, 74-58=16 and 107-91=16, which are unequal. The vertical fit returns null, and the horizontal fit fails on overlaps, so the list ends up with no layout. If the boxes were known (all 33 tall, gap 0), it would fit VERTICAL with spacing 0.

The page looks right, so this costs editability and Auto Layout, not looks. That fits medium for a very common AI-generated sidebar, tab or menu with one highlighted item.

The second piece of evidence (layout-zorder-transforms "Settings") is wrong. There the parent is `aside.h-56 overflow-y-auto`, a 224px-high clipping frame whose content is 315px tall. fitLayout fails on `end < -T` (224-270-45 = -91) whatever the last row's box is, so the proposed fix would not restore that layout. It is a separate scroll-overflow gap. Figma allows a fixed-height clipping frame with auto layout and overflowing content, so it is worth its own finding.

The proposed fix is sound in principle but under-specified. It does not say that the lifted single-child wrapper (the `<li>`) shifts k.x/k.y but would leave `outer` unshifted. It also does not handle display:inline elements, whose padded rect overlaps neighbouring lines, or remove the helper fields before the tree is posted. Below is a corrected, low-risk version that only runs where the plain fit already fails.

title: ::placeholder styling partly ignored (only color is taken)
evidence: gen-tw-controls: 'placeholder:italic placeholder:text-slate-400' shows italic 'you@company.com' in the original and upright text in the render. The segment's font.italic is false in gen-tw-controls.json.
rootCause: ui.html formNode() → toSegments([{raw:text, el}], placeholderColor): segStyle() reads font, weight, size, letter-spacing and text-transform from the input's own computed style. Only the color is overridden from css(el,'::placeholder'), and ::placeholder opacity is ignored.
verifierNotes:
I checked the code and the existing harness output, and the gap is real.

Code: in ui.html, formNode() calls `toSegments([{ raw: text, el }], placeholder ? css(el, '::placeholder').color : null)`. toSegments() then runs `const cs = css(r.el)`, which is the input's own computed style. segStyle(el, cs, colorOverride) reads fontStyle, fontWeight, fontSize, letterSpacing, lineHeight and textTransform from that style. The placeholder pseudo contributes only its color, and its opacity is never read.

Harness evidence: in dev/out/gen-tw-controls.json, the 'you@company.com' segment has font.italic=false and weight 400. Its fill is slate-400, (0.565,0.631,0.725), which shows the color override does work. In orig.png the placeholder is clearly italic; in render.png it is upright. The case uses `placeholder:text-slate-400 placeholder:italic` on a Tailwind input, so this is not a renderer artifact.

Impact is low: AI pages often style placeholder color but rarely change its font. The mismatch is cosmetic, a slant or weight difference inside empty inputs.

The proposed fix is basically right, but it has two flaws:
1. `parseFloat(pcs.opacity) || 1` turns opacity 0, a deliberately hidden placeholder (a common floating-label pattern), into 1.
2. It suggests adding a new styleSrc parameter. segStyle already takes cs as an argument; only toSegments hard-codes css(r.el), so the change is smaller than proposed.

Chrome's getComputedStyle(el,'::placeholder') returns full inherited values (font-*, color, opacity, letter-spacing, text-transform, line-height), so reading everything from the pseudo is safe. Only the agent changes; code.js already handles italic, weight and opacity per segment, so nothing new is needed on the Figma API side.

title: Input text ignores text-align (OTP boxes, quantity steppers and amount fields come out left-aligned)
evidence: gen-mobile-verify@390: the OTP digits '4','8','1' (text-align:center) sit at the left edge of their 48px boxes. The quantity '2' is left-aligned instead of centered between −/+. '$1,250.00' (text-align:right) is at the left instead of the right. Compare orig and render PNGs.

verifierNotes:
Confirmed by reading the code and re-running the case. In ui.html formNode(), every non-TEXTAREA control gets its text from textNode(segs, {x: cb.x-rect.left, ..., align: 'LEFT', autoResize: 'WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT'}). cs.textAlign is only read on the TEXTAREA branch. In code.js, shapeNode() and createText() pass n.align straight to textAlignHorizontal, so the hard-coded LEFT goes all the way into Figma. This is not a renderer artifact. I re-ran `node dev/fidelity.mjs gen-mobile-verify -w 390` (diff 2.32%, 0 mock errors). In orig.png the OTP digits 4/8/1 are centered in their 48px boxes, the stepper's '2' is centered and '$1,250.00' is right-aligned. In render.png all of them hug the left content edge. The proposed fix is basically right but has two problems:
1. It switches to a fixed-width box with autoResize 'HEIGHT' with no overflow guard. Inputs never wrap. When the value or placeholder is wider than the content box (long placeholders in narrow inputs are common), or when Figma's font metrics come out a little wider than Chrome's, a HEIGHT-mode text layer wraps onto two or more lines. Today's WIDTH_AND_HEIGHT path does not have that problem, so the fix would cause a regression.
2. ALIGN maps 'justify' to JUSTIFIED. A single-line input renders justify as start, so it should map to LEFT here.

Also, no special case is needed for input[type=submit|button|reset]. Chrome's UA sheet already gives them text-align:center, so reading cs.textAlign covers them.

- A number input keeps space for the spin button inside its content box, so the centered '2' in Chrome sits about 6-7px left of the content-box center. That residual is small.
- The empty type=date input (Chrome shows 'дд.мм.гггг') produces no text at all. That is a separate gap.
